instructions: Spoon the 1/3 cup of yogurt into a large bowl. If there's liquid on top, pour it off first so the marinade stays thick.

Grate the garlic and the 2 tsp of ginger into the bowl. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze one half in, about 2 tbsp. Add 1 tbsp of the oil, the chili powder, garam masala, coriander, turmeric, pepper and salt. Stir until smooth.

Pat the 1.5 lbs of cod dry with paper towels and cut it into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Add them to the bowl and turn gently until every piece is coated. Let it sit for 15 minutes. Don't leave it longer, or the fish turns mushy.
Meanwhile, cut the other lemon half into wedges.
Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium for a minute, then add the remaining 2 tbsp of oil. Lift the fish out of the bowl and lay the pieces in a single layer with a little space between them.

Cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and the pieces lift easily. Turn each piece gently and cook the other sides for 3 minutes. You're cooking the fish to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Press a piece with a fork: it's done when it flakes easily.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Swasthi's Tandoori Fish Tikka (5 from 34 ratings) is a thick yogurt and garam masala marinade for 15 minutes to an hour, then cooked in the oven or pan-fried until it flakes. Yummy Tummy marinates longer with cumin, mint and cornstarch or gram flour and cooks skewers on a tawa, and both warn that marinating too long makes the fish mushy. This follows the lead's pan-fry method with 1 1/2-inch pieces for 1.5 lbs of cod and leaves out the optional peppers and onion.
